options.how: Production keeps running offline once unlocked, so a visit is a quick check-in to spend cookies on buildings and upgrades.
Campaigns can last dozens of hours; a 1936 start adds years of war preparation and prolongs an already lengthy game.

sources.note: Cookie Clicker: offline production unlocked and boosted by prestige upgrades
Hearts of Iron IV: campaigns last dozens of hours; 1936 start prolongs them

options.how: A full game is three rounds of typed answers and votes, listed by Jackbox at about 15 minutes for 3 to 8 players.
A season can take around 50 hours; pre-season tactics and training alone can fill five hours before the first match.

sources.note: Quiplash 3: listed duration 15 minutes, 3 to 8 players
Football Manager 2024: a season might take 50 hours; five hours of pre-season setup

options.how: Real-time matches are capped at five minutes including a two-minute overtime, so a session is one or two battles on a phone.
Start in 1939 with war already lined up, or in 1936 to build up yourself; either way a campaign is a multi-sitting commitment.

sources.note: Clash Royale: games are 5 minutes long, overtime 2 minutes
Hearts of Iron IV: 1936 or 1939 starts; campaigns last dozens of hours

options.how: One shared puzzle per day with six guesses; a session ends in minutes and the next one waits until midnight.
Engaging with every system stretches a season to 50 hours, and reviewers expect to sink hundreds of hours a year into it.

sources.note: Wordle: one word per day, six tries, deliberate daily limit
Football Manager 2024: season might take 50 hours; 300+ hours a year

options.how: A run of test chambers lasting roughly two to four hours that closes with its final chambers and the credits song Still Alive.
New challenge leagues launch about every 13 weeks with a fresh economy; characters later move into the permanent leagues.

sources.note: Portal: short campaign of test chambers
Path of Exile: challenge leagues every 13 to 16 weeks, fresh economy, transfer to permanent leagues

options.how: A three to four hour side-scrolling journey to a fixed ending, with a hidden alternate ending for players who find every secret.
Runs on the real clock and calendar; upgrades wait for real days to pass and there is no end game, only the island you shape.

sources.note: Inside: roughly three to four hour playthrough
Animal Crossing: New Horizons: real-time calendar, no end game

options.how: Eight worlds of four levels end when Mario frees the princess in World 8, then offer a harder second quest.
No win condition or ending: players set their own goals for a household that can keep living indefinitely.

sources.note: Super Mario Bros.: eight worlds of four levels, princess rescued in World 8, new quest
The Sims: open-ended sandbox without set goals or a way to win

options.how: About two hours of family vignettes, paced to be finished in a single sitting like a film.
Over 17,000 levels and counting, with new batches added every week, so the saga map never runs out.

sources.note: What Remains of Edith Finch: short runtime compared to a film
Candy Crush Saga: about 17,000 levels, new levels each week

options.how: Career mode is a ladder of song tiers, each capped by an encore; clearing every tier completes the career.
Every beatmap is community-made, so the song library grows constantly, with ranked maps feeding leaderboards.

sources.note: Guitar Hero: career tiers with encores; finishing all tiers completes Career mode
osu!: beatmaps are created and uploaded by the community, ranked for leaderboards

options.how: A roughly eight-hour descent through a castle that ends in one of three endings decided in the final room.
A live service that keeps adding chapters with new killers and survivors, still on a yearly roadmap at its 10th anniversary.

sources.note: Amnesia: The Dark Descent: length and three endings
Dead by Daylight: 10th anniversary roadmap of new chapters

options.how: Fights use paint guns and ink bombs in a cartoony city, so the only ESRB descriptor is Cartoon Violence (E10+).
Blood, gore and demonic horror are the selling point, and the store flags it for adult audiences.

sources.note: Splatoon: E10+, Cartoon Violence, paint guns and ink bombs
Doom (2016): content described as blood and gore, violence, language, horror

options.how: Shells and spin-outs with no injury; rated E and PEGI 3, with Smart Steering and Auto-Accelerate for young drivers.
Scores points for running down pedestrians; UK and German releases had to swap them for green-blooded zombies or robots.

sources.note: Mario Kart 8 Deluxe: ESRB E, PEGI 3, Smart Steering, Auto-Accelerate
Carmageddon: censored releases replaced pedestrians with zombies or robots

options.how: Zombies take whimsical hits from plants and their heads pop off cartoonishly, keeping it at E10+.
Heads and limbs are blown off and blood streaks the walls; rated M for blood and gore, intense violence and language.

sources.note: Plants vs. Zombies: E10+, cartoony zombie heads popping off
Left 4 Dead: M for blood and gore, intense violence, language

options.how: Mascot brawling for up to eight players on any stage, rated E10+ so families and tournament players share one game.
Mid-match Fatal Blows and gory Fatalities are showpieces, earning an M for blood and gore and intense violence.

sources.note: Super Smash Bros. Ultimate: ESRB E10+, up to eight players on all stages
Mortal Kombat 11: M for blood and gore, intense violence, strong language

options.how: Ghosts are stunned with a flashlight and vacuumed up, never killed, so a haunted house stays rated E.
Leans on strong horror themes, gore such as corpses, violence and strong language, aimed squarely at adults.

sources.note: Luigi's Mansion: ESRB E, flashlight and Poltergust 3000 capture ghosts
Amnesia: The Dark Descent: strong horror themes, gore, violence, strong language

options.how: No combat: players glide over sand and ruins alone or with a fellow traveler, and the store tags it Family Friendly.

options.game: The Last of Us Part I
options.how: Close-up stealth kills, dismemberment, themes of suicide and torture, and frequent strong language.

sources.note: Journey: exploration, solo or with a fellow traveler, Family Friendly tag
The Last of Us Part I: mature content description

options.how: Craft fly on realistic aerodynamic and orbital physics, so a rocket's design and maneuvers decide whether it reaches orbit.
Ships fly from deep space to a planet's surface with no loading screens; engine upgrades simply let you jump farther.

sources.note: Kerbal Space Program: realistic aerodynamic and orbital physics
No Man's Sky: seamless space to surface flight, upgrades to jump farther

options.how: Haul cargo across real European road networks and 60-plus cities in licensed MAN, Volvo and Mercedes-Benz trucks.
Crash anywhere at any time, wreck friends online and hunt jumps, stunts and shortcuts; destruction is the reward.

sources.note: Euro Truck Simulator 2: real road networks, 60+ cities, licensed trucks
Burnout Paradise: crash anywhere, wreck friends, stunts and shortcuts

options.how: Live real-world weather, a whole-planet map and a physics model with over 1000 control surfaces per plane.
A flight shooter tuned so anyone can enjoy blistering speed, 360-degree pursuits and strikes on land, sea and air targets.

sources.note: Microsoft Flight Simulator: live weather, whole planet, 1000+ control surfaces
Ace Combat 7: flight shooter with accessible handling, Arcade tag

options.how: A massive military sandbox sold on authentic, true combat gameplay across infantry and vehicle warfare.
Swaps bullets for paint guns and ink bombs in the cartoony city of Inkopolis, so every hit reads at a glance.

sources.note: Arma 3: massive military sandbox, true combat gameplay, authentic
Splatoon: paint guns and ink bombs in cartoony Inkopolis

options.how: Licensed courses, real pros including Tiger Woods, and a choice of analog Swing Stick or 3-Click swing.
Speed Golf has everyone sprint to their ball at once, and character Special Shots pierce straight through trees.

sources.note: PGA TOUR 2K23: licensed courses, real pros, Swing Stick and 3-Click swing
Mario Golf: Super Rush: Speed Golf, Special Shots pierce foliage

options.how: Deliveries cover thousands of miles of real road networks and landmarks, so the drive itself is the content.
Trailing racers get stronger items such as Lightning, and tricks off ramps grant a speed boost on landing.

sources.note: Euro Truck Simulator 2: thousands of miles of real road networks
Mario Kart Wii: lower places get stronger items, ramp tricks give boosts

options.how: VR only with tracked controllers: players physically slash, duck and dodge through every beat.
Circles are aimed with a mouse or tablet pen and hit with mouse clicks or the Z and X keys.

sources.note: Beat Saber: VR only, tracked controllers, slash, duck and dodge
osu!: mouse, Z and X keys, tablet or touchscreen input

options.how: Slice fruit tossed across a phone screen while avoiding bombs; the slice gesture is the whole control scheme.
An RTS rebuilt for the Xbox 360 controller, with a radial Circle Menu and base-centred economy replacing mouse micro.
Cross-platform lobbies mix Android, iOS, PC and console players in the same 4 to 15 player game.

sources.note: Fruit Ninja: slice fruit, don't slice bombs, on iPhone
Halo Wars: console RTS control scheme, Circle Menu, centralized interface
Among Us: 4 to 15 players, cross-platform play across mobile, PC and console

options.how: Steer by tilting the Wii Remote, usually in the bundled Wii Wheel, and flick it upward to trick off ramps.
The analog stick sets speed, so Mario can tiptoe past enemies or creep along narrow ledges; C-buttons turn the camera.

sources.note: Mario Kart Wii: tilt the remote to steer, Wii Wheel, shake for tricks
Super Mario 64: analog stick precision for tiptoeing, C-button camera

options.how: Couch co-op for up to four chefs who must communicate and coordinate to prep, cook and serve orders.
A four-player local archery brawler built around versus matches where players snatch arrows mid-flight.

sources.note: Overcooked: couch co-op for one to four players
TowerFall Ascension: 4-player local versus archery

options.how: A 1 to 4 player online co-op shooter where Scout, Gunner, Engineer and Driller split the work in destructible caves.
Fast real-time battles against players worldwide; every match is a short head-to-head duel.

sources.note: Deep Rock Galactic: 1-4 player co-op FPS, four classes
Clash Royale: real-time multiplayer battles against players worldwide

options.how: Single-player only: one explorer unpicks a solar system trapped in an endless time loop.
Players share server worlds grouped into data centers, busy enough that subscribers get priority login when congested.

sources.note: Outer Wilds: single-player, endless time loop
Final Fantasy XIV: worlds, data centers, priority login during congestion

options.how: Up to four players share one screen; a fallen player floats back in a bubble and teammates can carry each other.
Every stage supports up to eight players brawling at once on a single console.

sources.note: New Super Mario Bros. Wii: four-player shared screen, bubbles, carrying players
Super Smash Bros. Ultimate: all stages playable with up to eight players

options.how: Free to play; revenue comes from the cosmetic Item Shop and the battle pass.
Free to play; gacha banners with pity sell characters and weapons.
Premium purchase, later extended by the paid Shadow of the Erdtree expansion.

sources.note: Fortnite: battle pass and cosmetic rewards
Genshin Impact: official site
Elden Ring: Shadow of the Erdtree paid DLC expansion

options.how: Free worlds exist, but paid membership unlocks over three times the map, nine more skills and many more quests.
Completely free and never pay to win; the shop sells armour and weapon effects, pets and stash tabs.
Bought up front, then extended by the paid Booster Course Pass that added tracks across 2022 and 2023.

sources.note: Old School RuneScape: membership plans and members-only content
Path of Exile: completely free, never pay to win
Path of Exile: shop categories of effects, pets, stash tabs
Mario Kart 8 Deluxe: Booster Course Pass paid DLC

options.how: Free, but sells extra moves, extra lives, boosters and gold bars to push past hard levels.
Free with no paywalls or timers; video ads grossed over $1 million alongside optional cosmetic characters.
One up-front price with no DLC or in-app purchases.

sources.note: Candy Crush Saga: free, sells extra moves, lives, boosters, gold bars
Crossy Road: no paywalls, cosmetic characters, video ads grossed over $1 million
Papers, Please: paid up front, no DLC or in-app purchases

options.how: Earned from in-app advertising, reportedly $50,000 a day in ad revenue at its peak.
Free to play; random five-card packs sell for gold or real money, with a Legendary guaranteed within 40 packs.

sources.note: Flappy Bird: $50,000 a day in ad revenue
Hearthstone: random packs for gold or money, 40-pack Legendary pity
Hearthstone: free-to-play digital collectible card game

options.how: LocalThunk built it alone as a side project from late 2021, handling design, code and art himself.
Innersloth shipped the 2018 mobile release with three people, bringing in an artist later.
About 1,600 staff worked directly on it across Rockstar's studios, and over 3,000 people touched it in all.

sources.note: Balatro: solo developer LocalThunk
Among Us: made by three people, Amy joining later for art
Red Dead Redemption 2: about 1,600 directly on development, roughly 2,000 in total

options.how: Lucas Pope designed, coded and drew it alone, about nine months from first mockups to release.
Supergiant grew to a core team of seven, including the narrator, working largely from a house.
Rockstar North's 360-person core team pulled in Rockstar studios worldwide, over 1,000 people in all.

sources.note: Papers, Please: solo developer, about nine months to release
Bastion: core team of seven including the principal voice actor
Grand Theft Auto V: over 1,000 people across Rockstar studios

options.how: Daisuke Amaya wrote everything himself over five spare-time years, about two years of actual work.
Two ex-2K Shanghai developers, one on art and design and one on code and design, funded by Kickstarter.
Built in house by Motion Twin, a worker cooperative of roughly eight to eleven people.

sources.note: Cave Story: Amaya wrote everything himself; five years, about two of real work
FTL: two-person Subset Games, side project from 2K Shanghai
Dead Cells: Motion Twin cooperative team size

options.how: Zeekerss made and keeps updating it alone, and prefers to stay solo rather than gather a team.
House House's four members decide direction by consensus, with outside help on 3D art and sound.

sources.note: Lethal Company: solo developer Zeekerss, prefers to work solo
Untitled Goose Game: four-person House House, consensus decisions

options.how: Dong Nguyen built it in under three days, the length of a game jam, reusing a bird from a cancelled project.
Hipster Whale aimed for six weeks and shipped in 12, keeping the bet small so a flop would cost little.
Five years at Polytron, with almost none of the first two years' work surviving into the final game.

sources.note: Flappy Bird: created in less than three days
Crossy Road: made in 12 weeks, set out to make it in six
Fez: five-year development at Polytron

options.how: Started mid-January 1992 on existing Catacomb 3D tech and shipped in May, a four to six month cycle.
Work began in late 1992 and the shareware episode shipped December 10, 1993, after slipping a Q3 target.
Began as a 2007 hobby project and shipped in 2016 after repeated reworks, nearly a decade in development.

sources.note: Wolfenstein 3D: four-month development
Doom: late 1992 start, December 10, 1993 release
Owlboy: decade-long development from 2007

options.how: Team Meat took 18 months from first engine code to XBLA certification, stretched by content creep.
Conceived in 2010, delayed past a 2014 target, and shipped in 2017 after the founders quit jobs and remortgaged homes.

sources.note: Super Meat Boy: 18 months of development
Cuphead: began 2010, founders quit jobs and remortgaged houses

options.how: Made in GameMaker by one developer, growing out of a battle system prototype he programmed first.
Programmed in Lua on the LOVE framework rather than a full engine, with readable shipped source that modders build on.
Two-person Bytten Studio used Godot, patching engine code for frame rate and partnering out console ports.

sources.note: Undertale: built in GameMaker
Balatro: made with the Lua-based LOVE framework, not a mainstream engine
Cassette Beasts: Godot showcase interview

options.how: Moon Studios chose Unity for its extensible editor and moved to Unity 5 for seamless level streaming at 60fps.
Acquire leaned on Unreal Engine 4's 3D lighting and effects around 2D sprites, the basis of its HD-2D look.

sources.note: Ori and the Blind Forest: Unity, move to Unity 5 for streaming
Octopath Traveler: UE4 and HD-2D

options.how: A small-team 2D arena roguelite built in Godot that juggles large counts of enemies, projectiles and pickups.
Nolla wrote its Falling Everything engine in C++ to simulate every pixel, with Box2D rigid bodies on top.

sources.note: Brotato: listed among acclaimed Godot games
Noita: GDC talk on its custom falling sand engine

options.how: Colossal Order built it in Unity, switching to Unity 5 late in the beta and keeping it for the whole project.
Built in Unreal and moved to Unreal Engine 5 in Update 8, gaining Lumen lighting and World Partition streaming.
Re-Logic wrote it in C# on Microsoft's XNA framework instead of licensing a commercial engine.

sources.note: Cities: Skylines: Unity case study, switch to Unity 5 near the end of beta
Satisfactory: Update 8 moves the game to Unreal Engine 5
Terraria: coded in Microsoft XNA

options.how: A 2D sprite platformer on a flat plane where each level ends at the Giant Gate.
Keeps side-scrolling 2D play but renders characters and elements as 3D models: a 2.5D Mario.
Free 3D movement through open courses, with a Lakitu-operated camera the player can rotate and zoom.

sources.note: Super Mario World: 2D platformer, goal is the Giant Gate
New Super Mario Bros.: side-scrolling 2.5D, first 2D Mario with 3D models
Super Mario 64: 3D platformer, Lakitu camera

options.how: Flat 2D sprite levels on a single plane, small enough for one person to draw and build alone.
HD-2D: retro pixel sprites placed in polygonal 3D environments with modern lighting and depth effects.
A fully 3D solar system whose planets are packed with hidden locations to reach and explore.

sources.note: Cave Story: 2D game made by one developer
Octopath Traveler: 3D environments combined with 2D pixels
Outer Wilds: explore a solar system of planets
